reason: The hypothesis relies on a single study (PMC8709257) which directly supports the key premises: the coatings were prepared on Zr-alloy, Al content affected properties, 10.2 at.% Al gave the best corrosion resistance via a dense oxide layer, and the work targets accident-tolerant fuel. The hypothesis accurately represents these findings, though it generalizes 'corrosion resistance' to 'high-temperature oxidation resistance' and 'delayed fuel rod swelling explosion', which are slight overstatements not fully covered by the cited evidence.
premises: AlNbTiZr MEA coatings can be deposited on Zr-alloy substrates
Al content influences coating microstructure and properties
A specific Al content (10.2 at.%) yields the best corrosion resistance in the cited study
Improved corrosion resistance is due to a denser oxide layer of Nb2Zr6O17 and ZrO2
